noInherit.description: If true, the annotation is not inherited by mixins.

hyperparameter.description:
Mark fields on sub-types of {@link MlAtomicPipe} as hyperparameters. These fields / hyperparameters can then
be addressed using the {@MlPipe#withHyperparams} API, creating a new copy of the {@link MlPipe} that includes the
new or updated hyperparameters.

containsHyperparams.description:
Mark fields on sub-types of {@link MlAtomicPipe} as a field whose Type contains
hyperparameters. Then, the nested fields, or nested hyperparameters, can be
referenced and modified using the hyperparameter APIs on {@link MlPipe}.

Use the dot delimiter ('.') to address nested hyperparameters when calling {@link MlPipe} APIs.
Example for field that is {@link Obj}:
```py
keras_pipe = c3.MlPipe.convert(model)
keras_pipe.generator.batchSize
>>> 32
keras_pipe = keras_pipe.withHyperparams({'generator.batchSize': 64})
keras_pipe.generator.batchSize
>>> 64
```

Additionally, if the field contains an {@link Array} or {@link Map}, then the dot notation can be used to
access the collection value by position and key, respectively.
For example, suppose a pipe has the following field:
```
@ML(containsHyperparams=true)
mapp: map<string, int>
```
Then `withHyperparams` can be used to change an existing key within the map or adding a non-existing one:
```
pipe = pipe.withHyperparams({"key": 42})
```
